title: LR
summary: Logical Reasoning. How to master LR: Argument Structure, Reasoning Structure, Trap Answers. Question Family: Assumption (64%), Inference (24%), Function (19%).

title: LR Overview（總覽）
summary: Three question families by share of the test; difficulty rises with question number.

blocks.text: Assumption family 64%; Inference family 24%; Function family 19%.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: Difficulty by position (PT62 to PT81): Q1 to Q8 intuitive; Q9 to Q16 trap answers dominate; Q17 to Q25 reasoning structures plus trap answers.
blocks.label: Recognition

blocks.text: Evidence, Assumption, Conclusion. Example: "Blue cars are the fastest cars on the road. Therefore, you should buy a blue car." The assumption bridges evidence to conclusion.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: Identify the task in the stem before reading the stimulus for structure.
blocks.label: Steps

title: Assumption Family（假設家族）
summary: Flaw 16%, Necessary Assumption 11%, Weaken 9%, Principle 9%, Strengthen 7%, Paradox 7%, Sufficient Assumption 4%.

blocks.text: Flaw 16%; Necessary Assumption（必要假設） 11%; Weaken 9%; Principle 9%; Strengthen 7%; Paradox 7%; Sufficient Assumption（充分假設） 4%.
blocks.label: Recognition

blocks.text: Necessary Assumption（必要假設）: pick the weakest link the argument cannot do without. Sufficient Assumption（充分假設）: pick the statement that fully closes the gap between premises and conclusion.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: Two tasks differ in direction. Necessary asks what must be true for the argument; Sufficient asks what would make the conclusion follow.
blocks.label: Why It Works

blocks.text: PT140 S1 Q16 (Necessary Assumption（必要假設）): correct answer allows "or" or "both"; reading it as "both required" makes the weakest link look too strong.
blocks.label: Official Example

blocks.text: Verified 2026-09-15 with reasoning stated (S1 Q16). Sufficient Assumption（充分假設） method taught on the spot (S3 Q11); independent verification still pending.
blocks.label: Status

title: Inference Family（推論家族）
summary: Most Supported 8%, Must Be True 7%, Paradox 7%, Must Be False 1%, Agree/Disagree 1%.

blocks.text: Most Supported（最受支持） 8%; Must Be True（必然為真） 7%; Paradox 7%; Must Be False（必然為假） 1%; Agree/Disagree（爭點） 1%.
blocks.label: Recognition

blocks.text: "Cannot be inferred" is not the same as "false". Must Be True（必然為真） and Most Supported（最受支持） reward what the premises support; Must Be False（必然為假） rewards what they contradict.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: Most Supported（最受支持） may be weaker than the premises but may not add more than the premises give.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: Agree/Disagree（爭點）: first screen for an option both speakers address; then screen for opposite positions on it.
blocks.label: Steps

blocks.text: PT140 S1 Q10 (Agree/Disagree（爭點）) answered with the two screens; PT140 S3 Q17 (Most Supported（最受支持）) missed by preferring a less absolute option and accepting "principally", which the premises never compared.
blocks.label: Official Example

blocks.text: Main Conclusion 3%; Role 3%; Method 5%; Parallel 3%; Parallel Flaw 4%.

title: Argument Structure（論證結構）
summary: Argument = Conclusion (verdict or judgment) supported by Premise (evidence or support). Three steps.

items: Find the Conclusion + Evidence: use keywords, Opinion vs Fact, the logic of Supported / Supporting.
Be Skeptical of the Conclusion: even though the Evidence is true, we can argue the Anti-Conclusion.
Pay Attention to Reasoning Patterns: Recommendations, Hypotheses, Rebuttals, Judgments, Predictions.

title: Find the Conclusion + Evidence（找結論與證據，用關鍵字）
summary: Find the verdict first, then the evidence that supports it; label everything else.

blocks.text: Five roles: Conclusion, Premise, Background, Opposing Position, Concession（讓步）.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: Keywords. Conclusion: so, thus, hence, therefore, as a result, this shows, consequently. Support: for, after all, because, since (FABS). Concession（讓步）: but, yet, however. Opinion: should, ought, clearly, obviously, evidently, apparently, probably. Opposing: attributions (most people think, some biologists say); concessions (granted, while, although, naturally, though it is true).
blocks.label: Recognition

blocks.text: A concession（讓步） ("although", "nevertheless", "admittedly") limits the position; it never supports the main conclusion.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: A rule stated as a premise ("Any X must Y") is evidence, not background. Ask: does the conclusion depend on it?
blocks.label: Trap

blocks.text: A compressed rebuttal ("This is a mistake.", "That view is wrong.") is the conclusion itself; the sentence after it is evidence, not the conclusion. Do not take the last factual sentence as the conclusion.
blocks.label: Trap

blocks.text: Reasoning patterns to recognise (Notes step 3): Recommendations, Hypotheses, Rebuttals, Judgments, Predictions. Match the skeptical question to the pattern.
blocks.label: Recognition

blocks.text: PT140 S2 Q16: compressed rebuttal conclusion missed in 2025 and again in 2026 (SIG-003). PT140 S3 Q12 and S1 Q09 answered correctly with reasons on 2026-09-14.
blocks.label: Official Example

blocks.text: Roles: verified 2026-09-13 to 09-15 (original and official). SIG-001 rule premise misread as background: delayed retest passed 2026-09-15. SIG-003: corrective taught, RC official check pending.
blocks.label: Status
Rule
blocks.text: Rule premises [Notes §Argument Structure; §Conditional]. A sentence containing must, only if, requires, necessary, unless, if...then, or any...that is a rule, not background. Stop and draw the arrow while reading.

items: Position does not decide role. Rules often sit in the last or first sentence next to the conclusion and are mistaken for part of it.
After drawing the arrow, see which end the conclusion is on: to deny something, use the contrapositive; to affirm, go forward.
Sufficient Assumption: the answer is the step from the factual premise to the rule's trigger. Delete options that restate a link already in the stimulus.
Necessary Assumption, Flaw, and Weaken: draw the arrow first; the rule is where the gap sits.
Backup when the signal word is missed: deletion test. Remove the sentence; if the path from facts to conclusion breaks, it is a premise.

blocks.label: Official Example
blocks.text: PT141 S2 Q10：規則在末句，訊號詞 must；bridge：discern → care。

blocks.label: Recognition
blocks.text: Direction words after an opposing view [Notes §Argument Structure 1, concession keywords]. When a sentence follows someone else's position, read its direction words before assigning it a side: only, merely (minimize), in any case, even if (independent of the preceding claim), despite, but (contrast). Main Conclusion answers must be stated in the stimulus; an evaluation the author never made is out.

blocks.label: Official Example
blocks.text: PT141 S2 Q11：only 淡化、in any case 獨立理由；支持句誤歸反方。

title: Skeptical of Conclusion（質疑結論）
summary: Even though the evidence is true, argue the Anti-Conclusion.

blocks.text: Plans / Recommendations: how could we go along with this plan but not achieve the goal or be better off? "Thus, we should do X" → X does not help or is a net negative. "Thus, if we want Y, we should do X" → X does not help us get Y. "Thus, if we want Y, we must do X" → there are other ways to get Y.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: Flaw and Weaken: state the gap in one sentence before reading options, then pick only the option that says that sentence. If none does, reread the options, not the stimulus.
blocks.label: Steps

blocks.text: "Fails to consider X" is a flaw only if X, when true, weakens the argument. "Takes for granted X" is a flaw only if the argument collapses when X is denied.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: SIG-004: correct reasoning not matched to the answer letter (two instances 2026-09-13; PT140 S4 Q15). Corrective: match the pre-phrase to the option text; for Function questions verify the option verb first.
blocks.label: Trap

blocks.text: PT140 S1 Q13 and S3 Q07 missed 2026-09-14; S1 Q06 reasoning pointed to D but C was filled in (letter mismatch, counted wrong).
blocks.label: Official Example

blocks.text: Plans/Recommendations three forms and Anti-Conclusion: from Notes, not yet verified on a question. SIG-004 near transfer passed (original), official untimed passed once (S4 Q25); timed verification pending.
blocks.label: Status

title: Reasoning Structures（推理結構）
summary: Three structures with a fixed question for each: Conditional, Comparison, Causation.

blocks.text: Conditional: A → B, B → C, therefore A → C. Causal: A causes B, B causes C, therefore A causes C. Comparative: A < B, B < C, therefore A < C.
blocks.label: Recognition

blocks.text: Conditional: find the assumed conditions. Comparison: find differences (Analogy) or pros vs cons (Recommendation). Causation: ask for alternative explanations.
blocks.label: Rule

title: Conditional（條件）
summary: Find the assumed conditions. Arrow points at the necessary condition.

blocks.text: The author assumes "if X, then Y". Example: evidence "60% of the technicians are not certified"; conclusion "60% are unqualified"; assumed: if uncertified, then unqualified.
blocks.label: Recognition

blocks.text: Un-triggered conditionals: a stated rule whose trigger the evidence never establishes. Example: "audiences don't care what happens to any characters → not succeed as drama"; evidence only says audiences cannot discern personalities; the link "cannot discern → do not care" is assumed.
blocks.label: Recognition

blocks.text: If X then Y: X → Y. The necessary condition sits at the arrow tip. Contrapositive: negate both and reverse (not Y → not X). Converse and inverse do not follow.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: Necessary-condition wording: "X is essential / necessary / required for Y" gives Y → X. "Y requires X", "Y only if X" gives Y → X. "Unless X, Y" gives not X → Y.
blocks.label: Recognition

blocks.text: Negating "A and B" gives "not A or not B".
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: Quantifiers: all and no statements chain; most and some do not chain against the arrow. A "some" statement may be read in either direction but cannot be combined with another "some" or "most".
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: Corrected rule (was: "the group at the arrow tip is always larger"): for an all-statement A → B, every A is a B, so the B group is at least as large as the A group. This says nothing about size for most or some statements, and nothing when the arrow comes from a single conditional claim rather than a universal.
blocks.label: Rule

items: Sufficient Assumption（充分假設） three steps: write the premise chain as arrows.
Write the conclusion as an arrow.
Compare; the correct option is the missing link, often stated as its contrapositive（逆否）.

blocks.text: Turning natural English "if not X then not Y" into an arrow: not X → not Y, contrapositive（逆否） Y → X. Direction reversed on PT140 S3 Q11.
blocks.label: Trap

blocks.text: PT140 S1 Q17 (contrapositive（逆否） applied, correct); S3 Q11 (Sufficient Assumption（充分假設）, direction reversed, method taught on the spot); S3 Q17 (necessary read as "principally").
blocks.label: Official Example

blocks.text: Symbolised conditionals and contrapositive（逆否）s: verified. Natural-English necessary-condition cues and Sufficient Assumption（充分假設） direction: pending independent verification (Phase One week 1 focus). SIG-005 "some" against the arrow: delayed retest passed 2026-09-15.
blocks.label: Status
Rule
blocks.text: Sufficient vs. Necessary Assumption [補充]. 邏輯強度：一項陳述排除的可能情況越多，其強度越高。橋接陳述（bridge statement）：恰能連接前提與結論的最低限度陳述，同時為充分且必要。

items: Sufficient Assumption：強度大於或等於 bridge 者皆合格。Bridge Test：加入該選項後，結論是否必然成立。選項強度超過所需並非刪除理由。
Necessary Assumption：強度小於或等於 bridge 者皆合格。Negation Test：否定該選項後，論證是否瓦解。
類比：購買一美元商品，持有一百萬美元為充分而非必要；持有至少一美元為必要而未必充分。
題幹辨識：if assumed、allows、enables、logically follows 為 SA；depends upon、requires、the argument assumes 為 NA。
不在強度軸上的選項（需題文外事實才起作用）兩題型皆不收。

blocks.label: Official Example
blocks.text: PT141 S2 Q12：以 NA 判準刪除 SA 正解（most consented）。PT140 S3 Q11：SA 結論方向。

title: Comparison（比較）
summary: Find differences for Analogy; find pros vs cons for Recommendation.

blocks.text: "What is true in Case A should be true in Case B." Meaningful Distinctions: make it seem that the two cases are unfair to compare. "X is better than Y / we should do X / X is a net gain": Pros > Cons, we need to know and rank upsides and downsides.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: To defeat an analogy, the difference must bear on the standard of comparison. A difference that does not touch the standard is irrelevant.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: PT140 S1 Q10: meaningful distinction was the third screen; user could not state it and it was taught.
blocks.label: Official Example

blocks.text: Taught 2026-09-15; independent verification pending.
blocks.label: Status

title: Causation（因果）
summary: Ask: is there an alternative explanation?

blocks.text: Correlation: "people who are X are more likely than others to be Y" (X ¦ Y). Author's explanation: "clearly, X contributes to Y" (X → Y). Alternate explanations: Reverse Causality (X ← Y); Third Factor (Z → X and Z → Y). Plausibility of the author's explanation: was the suspect at the scene? more data to corroborate?
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: Anti-Causal 1, Could Have Been Worse: "took prep course X and scored only 150, thus the course did nothing" ignores the counterfactual. Anti-Causal 2, Unfair Comparison: "Bob took course X while Sharon self-studied; both got 150; thus the course did nothing" ignores different initial reference points.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: Working list of alternatives used in teaching: reverse causation, third factor, coincidence or small sample, selection. Notes name the first two; the last two are Supplement.
blocks.label: Recognition

blocks.text: A randomised controlled trial removes selection and reverse causation; it does not remove a third factor introduced after randomisation.
blocks.label: Recognition

blocks.text: SIG-002: alternative-explanation labels used imprecisely (third factor vs selection). Name the mechanism, not just "another cause".
blocks.label: Trap

blocks.text: Verified with original items 2026-09-14 (SIG-002 near transfer pending). Anti-Causal 1 and 2 not yet verified on a question.
blocks.label: Status

title: Eliminate Trap Answers（排除誘答）
summary: Wrong answers fail on Scope, Logic, or Degree. Eliminate on textual grounds only.

blocks.text: Six trap categories. Scope: Out of Scope（超出範圍）, Half Scope（只對一半）. Logic: Premise Support（只支持前提）, Reversal（方向顛倒）. Degree: Too Weak（太弱）, Too Strong（太強）.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: Withdrawn rule: "the shorter or weaker option wins". This is not a criterion. Eliminate an option only when the premises give it no support; support may come from several premises together.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: Degree: absolute wording is not the same as too strong. Judge only whether the premises support the claim. "Necessary" is not "principal"; a comparative word the premises never made ("principally", "mainly") is unsupported.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: PT140 S3 Q17: the correct option used absolute wording supported by the chain; the chosen option added "principally".
blocks.label: Official Example

blocks.text: Six-category names from Notes. Degree rule taught 2026-09-15; withdrawn rule documented.
blocks.label: Status

title: RC
summary: Reading Comprehension. Read for purpose and viewpoint; answer from the text.

items: Active Reading
Main Point
Passage Map
Trap Answers

title: RC Overview（總覽）
summary: Four passages, one comparative. Questions: Inference (78%), Purpose (17%), Assumption (5%).

blocks.text: Difficulty rises with complex language and with many viewpoints. Simple language with one viewpoint is easiest; complex language with many viewpoints is hardest.
blocks.label: Recognition

blocks.text: Passage first (read the whole passage, map it, then answer) is the training default. Question-first will be tested as a comparison in the second round of single-passage drills.
blocks.label: Steps

blocks.text: Reading time baseline (2026-09-16): P2 full reread 10 min, P1 local 3 min, P3 local 3 min.
blocks.label: Status

title: The RC Process（閱讀流程）
summary: Four steps: Active Reading, Main Point, Passage Map, Questions.

title: Step 1: Active Reading（主動閱讀）
summary: (1) Connect; (2) Anticipate where the passage is going.

blocks.text: Anticipating where the passage is going (Notes Step 1) is a reading action. Forming a direction before reading answer choices is a separate answering action. Do both; do not confuse them.
blocks.label: Rule

title: Step 2: Main Point（主旨）
summary: Common locations: end of P1 and start of P2, or start of the last paragraph.

blocks.text: Location is a heuristic, not a definition. The main point is the author's own claim that the rest of the passage serves. It may carry qualifiers.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: Corrected rule (was: "the main point must be unconditional"): a qualified claim can be the main point when the evidence serves it. A hedged downstream consequence ("if this is right, then ...") is EXTEND, not the main point.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: Test: ask what every paragraph is doing for. If a candidate sentence is only served by one paragraph, it is a sub-point.
blocks.label: Steps

blocks.text: PT140 S4 Q20 (Main Point) answered correctly 2026-09-14; 2025 miss was an unread author stance.
blocks.label: Official Example

blocks.text: Verified on two original passages and one official (2026-09-14).
blocks.label: Status

title: Step 3: Passage Map（文章地圖）
summary: Focus on the purpose of each paragraph; how the rest combines to lead to the main point.

blocks.text: Seven paragraph-function labels: INTRO, VIEW, COUNTER, SUPPORT, EVAL, AUTHOR, EXTEND. No other label set is used.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: One structure shown in the Notes: Opposing Point → Support for Opposing Point → Evidence Against Opposing Point → Main Point. Map the paragraphs, then locate where the author's main point sits.
blocks.label: Recognition

blocks.text: COUNTER presents an opposing view or objection (someone's position). EVAL is the author weighing a view. When one paragraph both reports and judges, label it by the sentence that carries the judgment.
blocks.label: Recognition

blocks.text: Ownership (whose view is speaking): attribution markers ("some historians", "on this view", "according to") hand the microphone to a source; the author takes it back with a pivot ("but", "however"), an evaluative word, or an unattributed conclusion. Tests: trace back to the owner; ask whether the author endorses it.
blocks.label: Steps

blocks.text: Map only to the resolution the questions need. A label per paragraph is usually enough; do not label every sentence.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: Passage map verified on PT140 S4 P1 and P3 (2026-09-15, 09-16).
blocks.label: Status

title: Step 4: Questions（作答）
summary: Inference 77.6%, Purpose 17.3%, Assumption 5.2%. Form a direction, then verify against the text.

items: Read the stem; name the task.
Form a direction before reading choices (not a full prediction for every question).
For Function and Attitude questions, check the option verb against the text first; if the text never does that action, eliminate.
Read the full proposition: who did what, scope, qualifiers.
Support may be several sentences combined; eliminate only when no textual support exists.

blocks.text: This sequence is a training scaffold; the goal is to fade it, not to run it on every question in the exam.
blocks.label: Why It Works

blocks.text: Withdrawn rule: "prefer the shorter or weaker option". Not a criterion.
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: Answer-choice verification taught 2026-09-15 (HO-008); applied on S4 Q25, Q26.
blocks.label: Status

title: Question types（題型）
summary: Twelve RC question types with their share of RC questions.

blocks.text: Inference 27.6%; Opinion 22.2%; Purpose 13.0%; Main Point 12.3%; Meaning in Context 6.4%; Organization 4.3%; Analogy 3.7%; Most Supported（最受支持） 3.0%; Weaken 2.7%; Application 2.3%; Strengthen 2.0%; Principle 0.5%.
blocks.label: Recognition

title: Author Opinion / Attitude（作者態度）
summary: Identify whose judgment it is; determine its direction, then its strength.

items: Whose judgment: author or a reported source?
Direction: approving, disapproving, or neutral report.
Strength: hedge present (qualified, cautious) or no hedge (clear endorsement or dismissal).

blocks.text: When the author has a stance, do not choose a neutral descriptor ("subject to debate", "undecided"). Neutral is correct only when the author reports without evaluating.
blocks.label: Trap

blocks.text: Attitude vocabulary: dismissive（不屑、否定）, skeptical（懷疑）, qualified approval（有保留的贊同）, cautious（謹慎）, ambivalent（正反並存）, neutral（中立、只報導不評價）, critical（批評）, enthusiastic（熱切贊同）. Each needs a supporting sentence in the passage; if none exists the word is not supported.
blocks.label: Recognition

title: Primary Purpose（文章目的）
summary: What the whole passage does, covering every body paragraph.

blocks.text: Describing can be a purpose. In a descriptive passage with no rebuttal or proposal, the correct option is the description that covers all body paragraphs; an option that covers one paragraph but sounds like an argument is Out of Scope（超出範圍） (partial).
blocks.label: Rule

blocks.text: Topic area does not determine structure; do not infer "descriptive" from "humanities".
blocks.label: Trap

blocks.text: For "A does X while B does Y" or two-part options, verify both halves separately (Half Scope（只對一半） candidate, PT140 S4 Q12).

title: Local Purpose / Function（局部功能）
summary: Why the author includes a sentence or paragraph.

blocks.text: Check the option verb first: does the text actually do that action (illustrate, concede, qualify, refute)? If not, eliminate before reading the noun phrase.

title: Detail / Locate Details（細節定位）
summary: Locate, then compare nouns and qualifiers.

items: Take the key noun from the stem and locate the original sentence.
Compare the option to that sentence noun by noun, including qualifiers.
Accept a reasonable paraphrase; reject a sentence that is in the passage but does not answer the stem.

title: Comparative Passages（比較文章）
summary: Two passages on one topic; questions ask about each and about the relationship.

blocks.text: Map both passages with the seven labels. If a passage has an AUTHOR paragraph, it has a stance. State the relationship as the two main points in plain words.

blocks.text: Two-part options ("A does X while B does Y"): verify each half against its passage.

title: Trap Answers（誘答）
summary: Named wrong-answer patterns seen in PT140 reviews.

items: Unsupported Comparison（無依據的比較）: the option ranks or compares two things the passage never compares (Notes example, Main Point question on code-switching).
Too Strong（太強）: stronger than the text supports (S4 Q25 option D).
Opposite（相反）: reverses the author's direction (S4 Q26 option C).
Out of Scope（超出範圍）, partial: covers one paragraph but sounds like the thesis (S4 Q1 option C).
Half Scope（只對一半）: one half of a two-part option is right, the other is not (S4 Q12, candidate).
Wrong Emphasis（重點錯置）: neutral descriptor when the author has a stance (2025 S4 Q20 option D).
Verb mismatch: the option names an action the text never performs (Function questions, S4 Q15).

blocks.text: Withdrawn rule: "shorter or weaker option wins". Eliminate only on missing textual support.
blocks.label: Rule
